<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par75 />others (cf. Nöldeke, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} xxx. 185), {{GHGheb|text=נַֽאֲנָה}} from {{GHGheb|text=אָוָה}}, not Pi‛lel of {{GHGheb|text=נאה}} = {{GHGheb|text=נאו}}; hence, according to {{GHGpar|23|d}}, {{GHGheb|text=נָאווּ|translate=they are beautiful}} (for {{GHGheb|text=נַֽאֲווּ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=52|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=10}}; but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=93|verse=5}}, where Baer requires {{GHGheb|text=נָֽאֲוָה}}, read {{GHGheb|text=נַֽאֲנָה}} with ed. Mant., Ginsb.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|y}}
8. The ''apocope'' of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} causes no further changes beyond the rejection of the {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִגָּל}} from {{GHGheb|text=יִגָּלֶה}}; in one verb ''middle guttural'', however, a form occurs with the {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} shortened to {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}}, viz. {{GHGheb|text=יִמַּח}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יִמָּח}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=109|verse=13}}, as in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}; but in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=תִּמָּֽח}} verse 14. Cf. bb.—The {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} {{GHGheb|text=נִגְלוֹת}} emphasizing an {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=6|verse=20}}, is very extraordinary; probably it is a subsequent correction of an erroneous repetition of {{GHGheb|text=הגלות}}.—The ''infin. constr.'' {{GHGheb|text=לְחֵֽרָאֹה}} occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=21}} for {{GHGheb|text=לְהֵֽרָאֹת}}; cf. above, n.—On the {{GHGterm|infinitive Niphʿal}} with the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} elided, see {{GHGpar|51|l}}.—The irregular {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽעֲלוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=3}} has probably arisen from a combination of the readings {{GHGheb|text=תַּֽעֲלוּ}} ({{GHGterm|Qal}}) and {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽעָלוּ}} ({{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}). Similarly the solecism {{GHGheb|text=נְמִבְזָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=9}} might be due to a combination of the ''participle fem. Niphʿal'' ({{GHGheb|text=נִבְּזָה}}, cf. {{GHGheb|text=נַחְלָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֶחְפָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=נַֽעֲשָׂח}}) with the {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} ({{GHGheb|text=מֻבְזָה}}); but it is more correct, with Wellhausen, to explain the {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}} from a confusion with {{GHGheb|text=נמס}} and to read, in fact, {{GHGheb|text=נִבְזָח וְנִמְאָ֫סָת}}.

{{center|III. ''On Piʿēl, Pôʿēl, Puʿal, and Hithpaʿēl.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|z}}
9. In the 1st and 2nd persons of the {{GHGterm|perfect Piʿēl}} the second syllable in most of the instances has {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} on the analogy of {{GHGterm|Qal}} (see f), as {{GHGheb|text=דִּמִּ֫יתָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִוִּ֫יתִי}}; always so in the first ''plur.'', and before ''suffixes'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=כִּסִּ֫ינוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=26}}, {{GHGheb|text=דִּכִּיתָ֫נוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=20}}. The form with {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}} is found only in the 1st ''sing.'' (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=4|verse=21}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=17|hidebook=1}} along with the form with ''î''). On the tone of the ''perf. consec. Pi‛el'' of {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, see {{GHGpar|49|k}}.—{{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} has (besides {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=16}}) as a rule {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=24}}). On the other hand, {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} always has {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עֻשֵּׂ֫יתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=15}}.—A 1st ''sing. perfect Pô‛ēl'' {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹשֵׂ֫תִי}} ( ={{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹוסֵיתִי}}) occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=13}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|aa}}
10. The ''infinitive absolute Piʿēl'' takes the form {{GHGheb|text=כַּלֵּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=קַוֵּה}} (like {{GHGheb|text=קַטֵּל}}, the more frequent form even in the strong verb, see {{GHGpar|52|o}}); with ''ô'' only in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=40|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=קַוֹּה}}; with ''ôth'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=3|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=עָרוֹת}} (cf. above, n). On {{GHGheb|text=הֹגוֹ}} and {{GHGheb|text=הֹרוֹ}}, ''infinitives absolute'' of the passive of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, not of ''Pô‛ēl'', see above, n.—As {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} {{GHGheb|text=חַכֵּי}} occurs in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=6|verse=9}} (only orthographically different from {{GHGheb|text=חַכֵּה}}, if the text is correct); {{GHGheb|text=לְכַלֵּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=24}} (on the {{GHGheb|text=א}} see rr); {{GHGheb|text=עַד־לְכַלֵּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=24|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=31|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, for which in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=13|verse=17.19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=9|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=עד־כַּלֵּה}} with ''infin. abs.''; in {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=עֻנּוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=132|verse=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|bb}}
11. The apocopated {{GHGterm|imperfect}} must (according to {{GHGpar|20|l}}) lose the {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}} of the second radical, hence {{GHGheb|text=וַיְצַו|translate=and he commanded}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּעַר}} (for {{GHGheb|text=תְּעָרֶה}}=''t<sup>e</sup>‛arrè'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=141|verse=8}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=20}}; even in the principal pause {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תְּגַֽל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=9}}; {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּתְגַּל|translate=and he uncovered himself}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=תִּתְרַע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=22|verse=24}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=1.7.8}}. With the lengthening of {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} to {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיְתָו|translate=and he made marks}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=14}} (but read with Thenius {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫תָף}}, and instead of the meaningless {{GHGheb|text=וַיְשַׁנּוֹ}}<!-- not a translation --> ''ibid.'' read {{GHGheb|text=וַיְשַׁן}}). In {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תִּתְגָּר}}, in close connexion, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=9.19}}; {{GHGheb|text=תִּשְׁתָּע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=10}}; according to ''Qimḥi'' also {{GHGheb|text=יִתְאָו}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּתְאָו}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=23|verse=3.6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=11|verse=17}}, whilst Baer and Ginsburg read with the best authorities {{GHGheb|text=יִתְאַו}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּתְאַו}} (but cf. König, ''Lehrgeböude'', i. 597).<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=34|verse=7}} f., according to verse 10, {{GHGheb|text=תִּתְאַוֻּ}} (={{GHGheb|text=תִּתְאַוּוּ}}) is intended to be read for {{GHGheb|text=תְּתָאוּ}} ({{GHGterm|imperfect Piʿēl}} from {{GHGheb|text=תָּאָה}}).</ref>—On {{GHGheb|text=אֲחַוְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=17}} (for {{GHGheb|text=אֲחַוְּךָ}}) cf. {{GHGpar|20|m}}; on {{GHGheb|text=אּכָלְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=3}}, see {{GHGpar|27|q}};<section end=par75 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
